To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of time of day and task features on vigilance performance are not independent and that the effects of task features are more apparent when vigilance performance is assessed in the evening than in the morning.
vigilance performance varies with the time of testing and that some aspects of the task are more influential in some time periods than others.

(a) vigilance decrements are not always present; (b) when vigilance decrements do occur, they may depend upon task and individual differences in the way they are expressed; (c) vigilance decremits may be more pronounced in the afternoon than the morning; and (d) the vigilance decrement is not a unitary phenomenon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of task features, time of day, and individual differences in vigilance performance.
the effects of several factors that have been found to influence performance on vigilance tasks and with the effects of time of day when the tasks are performed.
the effects of several factors on performance in vigilance tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vigilance is not constant over time and that the nature of vigilance depends on the task characteristics.
the effects of time-of-day on vigilance are complex and depend on the nature of the task.
the time of day effects in vigilance tasks are not a simple matter of performance being better in the morning than in the afternoon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the time of day effects on vigilance performance are not due to a general decrement in the efficiency of perceptual processing.
vigilance performance is not constant across the 24 hr, that the nature of the task and the time-of-day effects are related, and that the nature of time-of-day effects depends on the task.
the vigilance decrement is not a unitary phenomenon, but is affected by the time of day, the nature of the task, and the characteristics of the stimulus events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vigilance is a multifaceted construct that can be influenced by many factors.
vigilance performance depends on the characteristics of the task and the time of day.
task features and time of day interact in complex ways to affect the performance of vigilance tasks.
